sentences.text: It could be your commute to work, a trip into town or the way home.
Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand.
On these sorts of trips it's easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing scenery.
The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
P2 This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a familiar route.
P3 The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention.
When we travel down a well-known route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly.

translation.content:
P1 Think about driving a route that's very familiar. It could be your commute to work, a trip into
town or the way home. Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand. On
these sorts of trips it's easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing
scenery. The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
P2 This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a
familiar route.
P3 The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention. When we travel down a well-known
route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly. And afterwards,
when we come to think back on it, we can't remember the journey well because we didn't pay much
attention to it. So we assume it was shorter.

P1 设想一下，你正开车行驶在一条十分熟悉的路上。它可能是你上班的通勤路，可能是进城的一
趟，或是回家的路。无论是哪一条，路上的每一处弯道、每一个转角，你都了如指掌。开这类熟路
时，人很容易对驾驶本身走神，而对沿途掠过的风景也几乎不加留意。结果就是，你会觉得这趟路花
的时间，比它实际花的要少。
P2 这就是「熟路效应」：人们往往会低估走一条熟悉路线所需要的时间。
懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2015-english-two/section3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好
P3 这种效应源于我们分配注意力的方式。当我们沿着一条熟悉的路线行驶时，由于无需太过集中
注意力，时间似乎就过得更快。而事后，当我们回过头去回想这趟行程时，却记不太清了，因为当时
我们并没怎么留意它。于是，我们便想当然地以为这趟路花的时间更短。

Section II Part A (2)
Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark

Text 2
P1 For years, studies have found that first-generation college students – those who do not have a
parent with a college degree – lag other students on a range of education achievement factors. Their
grades are lower and their dropout rates are higher. But since such students are most likely to advance
economically if they succeed in higher education, colleges and universities have pushed for decades to
recruit more of them. This has created "a paradox" in that recruiting first-generation students, but then
watching many of them fail, means that higher education has "continued to reproduce and widen, rather
than close" an achievement gap based on social class, according to the depressing beginning of a paper
forthcoming in the journal Psychological Science.
多年来,研究发现第一代大学生——即父母均未获得大学学位的学生——在一系列教育成就因素上落后于
其他学生。他们的成绩更低,辍学率更高。但由于这类学生如果在高等教育中取得成功,最有可能在经济上
获得提升,因此数十年来,各高校一直在努力招收更多这样的学生。这造成了"一个悖论":招收第一代大学生,

即将发表在《心理科学》期刊上的一篇论文令人沮丧的开头所指出的那样。
P2 But the article is actually quite optimistic, as it outlines a potential solution to this problem,
suggesting that an approach (which involves a one-hour, next-to-no-cost program) can close 63 percent of
the achievement gap (measured by such factors as grades) between first-generation and other students.
但这篇文章实际上相当乐观,因为它概述了解决这一问题的潜在方案,表明一种方法(涉及一个一小时、几乎
零成本的项目)可以缩小第一代大学生与其他学生之间63%的成就差距(以成绩等因素衡量)。

was defined as not having a parent with a four-year college degree. Most of the first-generation students

26.Recruiting more first-generation students has____.
[ A ]reduced their dropout rates
[ B ]narrowed the achievement gap
[ C ]missed its original purpose
[ D ]depressed college students
招收更多第一代大学生已经____。
A) 降低了他们的辍学率 B) 缩小了成绩差距 C) 偏离了其初衷 D) 使大学生感到沮丧
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】Recruiting more first-generation students has____. 是带空格的陈述句，要求补全 "招收
行为带来的结果"，问的是文中明确陈述过的客观事实。
【拆句】Recruiting more first-generation students has____. 主干是动名词短语作主语 + 现在完
成时 has + 空缺，空缺承担谓语后半部分；考生只需把 Recruiting more first-generation
students 整体当主语看待，结构无陷阱。

【定位】This has created "a paradox" in that recruiting first-generation students, but then watching
many of them fail, means that higher education has "continued to reproduce and widen, rather
than close" an achievement gap based on social class, according to the depressing beginning
of a paper forthcoming in the journal Psychological Science.
这造成了一个 "悖论"：招收一代生、然后又看着许多人失败，意味着高等教育在基于社会阶
层的成绩差距上 "持续在复制和扩大，而非缩小"——这是《心理科学》一篇即将发表的论文
那段令人沮丧的开头给出的说法。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
原文明言一代生 their dropout rates are higher，根本未提招收行为降低了辍学率——
选项的 reduced their dropout rates 与原文事实相反。
B) 与原文相反
原文明言差距 continued to reproduce and widen, rather than close，而选项
narrowed the achievement gap 正好相反——差距是扩大、不是缩小。
C) ✓ 正确
colleges and universities have pushed for decades to recruit more of them ↔
missed its original purpose
预判 "招收偏离初衷" 与 missed its original purpose 直接对位——招生的 purpose 是
缩小差距，结果是差距 reproduce and widen，因此 missed 成立。
D) 偷换概念
原文 the depressing beginning of a paper 中的 depressing 修饰的是 paper 的
beginning（论文开头的论调令人沮丧），而非招生行为使学生情绪沮丧；depressed
college students 把 depressing 的修饰对象偷换成了 college students。
27.The authors of the research article are optimistic because____.
[ A ]their findings appeal to students
[ B ]the recruiting rate has increased
[ C ]the problem is solvable
[ D ]their approach is costless

A) 他们的研究发现对学生有吸引力 B) 招生率已经提高 C) 这个问题是可以解决的
D) 他们的方法是零成本的
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】The authors of the research article are optimistic because____. 中 because 引导一个明
确的因果，要求补全文中给出的原因，属于事实型因果。
【拆句】The authors of the research article are optimistic because____. 主干 The authors are
optimistic + because 引导原因状语从句的空缺；考生只需明确空缺补的是 "乐观的原
因"，结构无陷阱。

【定位】But the article is actually quite optimistic, as it outlines a potential solution to this problem,
suggesting that an approach (which involves a one-hour, next-to-no-cost program) can close
63 percent of the achievement gap (measured by such factors as grades) between first-
generation and other students.
但这篇文章其实相当乐观，因为它勾勒出一个针对这个问题的潜在解决方案——它建议一种
方法（包含一个仅一小时、几乎零成本的项目）可以缩小一代生与其他学生之间 63% 的成
绩差距。
【选项】A) 无中生有
原文从未提及研究 findings appeal to students 这层关于 "对学生有吸引力" 的内容；
文章谈的是研究本身的乐观，而非研究对学生的吸引力。
B) 无中生有
原文未提到任何 recruiting rate has increased 的事实，首段只说 colleges and
universities have pushed for decades to recruit more of them——是推动招生意
愿，而非招生率已上升；并且即便上升，也与作者乐观与否无关。
C) ✓ 正确
outlines a potential solution to this problem ↔ the problem is solvable
预判 "问题有解" 与 the problem is solvable 完全对位，且原文 potential solution 的
不确定性被 solvable 的 "可" 准确保留，无过度推断。
D) 过度推断
原文是 next-to-no-cost（"几乎" 零成本），而非完全无成本；approach is costless
把 "几乎零" 推向 "完全零"，越过了原文的程度边界。并且作者乐观的根本理由是 "问题
有解"，而不是 "方法零成本"——后者只是程序细节。

grant for undergraduates with financial need, while this was true only for 8.6 percent of the

recipients of Pell Grants, a federal grant for undergraduates with financial need ↔
are in need of financial support

believe + that 宾语从句；从句主语 first-generation students 后接空缺谓语，考生需找

因为美国的大学很少承认社会阶层会如何影响学生的教育经历，许多一代生缺乏对自己为何

P1 Even in traditional offices, "the lingua franca of corporate America has gotten much more

companies in 1990, we would see much less frequent use of terms like journey, mission, passion. There
were goals, there were strategies, there were objectives, but we didn't talk about energy; we didn't talk
about passion."
哈佛商学院教授Nancy Koehn说，即使在传统办公室里，"美国企业界的通用语言也比20年前变得更加感

P2 Koehn pointed out that this new era of corporate vocabulary is very "team"-oriented – and not
by coincidence. "Let's not forget sports – in male-dominated corporate America, it's still a big deal. It's

There are lots and lots of CEOs in very different companies, but most think of themselves as coaches

Koehn指出，这个企业词汇的新时代非常强调"团队"——这并非巧合。"我们不要忘记体育运动——在男

P1 Many people talked of the 288,000 new jobs the Labor Department reported for June, along

appears the economy is creating jobs at a decent pace. We still have a long way to go to get back to

P3 Before explaining the connection to the Obamacare, it is worth making an important distinction.
Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs. They take part-time work because
this is all they can get. An increase in involuntary part-time work is evidence of weakness in the labor
market and it means that many people will be having a very hard time making ends meet.

作。他们从事兼职工作是因为这是他们能得到的全部。非自愿兼职工作的增加是劳动力市场疲软的证据,这
意味着许多人将很难维持生计。

Directions:

Unfortunately, life is not a bed of roses. We are going through life facing sad experiences.
Moreover, we are grieving various kinds of loss: a friendship, a romantic relationship or a house. Hard
times may hold you down at what usually seems like the most inopportune time, but you should
remember that they won't last forever.
不幸的是，生活并非一帆风顺。我们在生活中会经历悲伤的遭遇。此外，我们还要承受各种各样的失去：
一段友谊、一段恋情或一所房子。艰难时刻可能会在看似最不合时宜的时候将你击垮，但你应该记住，它
们不会永远持续下去。
When our time of mourning is over, we press forward, stronger with a greater understanding and
respect for life. Furthermore, these losses make us mature and eventually move us toward future
opportunities for growth and happiness. I want to share these old truths I've learned along the way.
当我们的哀悼时期结束后，我们会继续前行，变得更加坚强，对生活有了更深刻的理解和尊重。而且，这
些失去使我们变得成熟，并最终引领我们走向未来成长和幸福的机会。我想分享这些我一路学到的古老

If you are surrounded by problems and cannot stop thinking about the past, try to focus on the
present moment. Many of us are weighed down by the past or anxious about the future. You may feel
guilt over your past, but you are poisoning the present with the things and circumstances you cannot
change. Value the present moment and remember how fortunate you are to be alive. Enjoy the beauty of
the world around and keep your eyes open to see the possibilities before you. Happiness is not a point
in the future and not a moment from the past, but a mindset that can be designed into the present.

Directions:
Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
P1 Think about driving a route that's very familiar. It could be your commute to work, a trip into
town or the way home. Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand. On
these sorts of trips it's easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing
scenery. The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
P2 This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a
familiar route.
P3 The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention. When we travel down a well-known
route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly. And afterwards,
when we come to think back on it, we can't remember the journey well because we didn't pay much
attention to it. So we assume it was shorter.

P1 设想一下，你正开车行驶在一条十分熟悉的路上。它可能是你上班的通勤路，可能是进城的一
趟，或是回家的路。无论是哪一条，路上的每一处弯道、每一个转角，你都了如指掌。开这类熟路
时，人很容易对驾驶本身走神，而对沿途掠过的风景也几乎不加留意。结果就是，你会觉得这趟路花
的时间，比它实际花的要少。
P2 这就是「熟路效应」：人们往往会低估走一条熟悉路线所需要的时间。

英语二真题(2015)
Section IV Part A
Directions:
Suppose your university is going to host a summer camp for high school students.
Write a notice to
1)briefly introduce the camp activities, and
2)call for volunteers.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your name or the name of your university.
Do not write your address. (10 points)

写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Notice
A summer camp for high school students will be held on our campus from July 20 to July 30. During these ten
days, participants will enjoy inspiring lectures, visit our laboratories, and take part in outdoor team activities,
which aim to broaden their horizons and enrich their vacation.
To make the camp a success, we sincerely call for volunteers. Volunteers will help guide the students, organize
activities, and keep order. Anyone who is patient, responsible, and warm-hearted is warmly welcomed. Those
interested may sign up by emailing summercamp@office.com before July 10.
The Organizing Committee June 25
